title: Coral and the Cipher
premise: When estate lawyer Ansel Hartwell is called to read the will of Coral Vane, the town's beloved founder who died thirty years ago, she discovers a document dated after the burial — and an exhumation order reveals the coffin is empty. Ansel's investigation pulls her into a conspiracy among the town's founding families, who staged Coral's death to smuggle her out of a murder charge, and into a slow-burning alliance with the town archivist, Elias Thorn, whose duty to preserve records conflicts with his growing love for her. As Ansel traces the cipher Coral left in her will, she learns the 'murder' was actually a cover-up of a death caused by the town's other founders — and that Coral may still be alive. In the end, Ansel must choose between exposing the truth and destroying the town: she publishes the cipher's confession, letting justice fall where it may, while Elias chooses her over the archive, and Coral, dying at last, signs her real name to everything.
about_author: Astrid Amberdale spent a decade as a probate clerk in coastal New England before turning to fiction, giving her mysteries an insider's eye for wills, deeds, and the secrets they bury. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where the fog does half her plotting for her.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ansel Hartwell's POV. A courier delivers a will for Coral Vane — dated eleven years after her death and burial. Ansel, unable to resist an impossible case, accepts it against her firm's advice. Emotional beat: cold professional curiosity masking a hunger for something that matters.

chapters.title: Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: Ansel petitions the court; Judge Merrick grants it with unsettling eagerness. At Graywater Cemetery, the vault is opened before a small crowd. The coffin is empty except for a sealed envelope bearing Ansel's name. Beat: public shock, private dread.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Envelope
chapters.summary: Alone in her office, Ansel opens the envelope: a page of symbols and one line — 'Only the reader of my will may read my life.' She recognizes the cipher style from town archives. Beat: exhilaration curdling into isolation as she realizes someone wanted her specifically.

chapters.title: Elias Thorn's Archive
chapters.summary: Ansel visits the town archive and meets Elias Thorn, guarded keeper of Graywater's records. He denies knowing anything but slips her a ledger page. POV shifts briefly to Elias, who recognizes the cipher and lies about it. Beat: first spark of wary attraction.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Ansel interviews the founding families — the Ashcombes, the Delacroixes, Mayor Penn — each with polished, identical stories of the night Coral supposedly died. Too identical. Beat: mounting suspicion dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: The slipped ledger page shows payments from the Vane estate to all three families, dated the week of the funeral. Ansel confronts Elias; he admits he recognized the cipher because his grandmother helped design it. Beat: betrayal, then uneasy partnership.

chapters.title: The Night of the Fire
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Coral's POV, thirty years ago: a boathouse fire, a body, Coral fleeing into the fog as her friends swear they'll protect her. Beat: terror and gratitude entangling into guilt.

chapters.title: A Body That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Present day: Ansel obtains the original coroner's report and finds the dental records were falsified by Dr. Ashcombe, now dead. Whoever burned wasn't Coral. Beat: the case pivots from fraud to murder.

chapters.title: Threats in Probate
chapters.summary: Mayor Penn offers Ansel a lucrative position to drop the will's validity challenge. She refuses; that night her office is ransacked and the cipher stolen. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Cipher
chapters.summary: Elias reveals his grandmother's cipher key book survived in the restricted stacks. Working through the night together, they decode the first passage: 'I did not kill him. They know I did not.' Beat: intimacy born of shared obsession.

chapters.title: The Man in the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Decoded pages identify the victim: Tobias Renner, a land surveyor who discovered the founders were forging property lines to steal waterfront lots. Coral witnessed his death — poisoned, not burned. Beat: grief for a stranger, fury at the town.

chapters.title: Judge Merrick's Debt
chapters.summary: Ansel digs into why Merrick fast-tracked the exhumation: his father was the fourth signer of the cover-up pact. Merrick wanted it found. He gives her the pact document — unsigned by one name. Beat: an ally inside the machine.

chapters.title: Penn's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Mayor Penn has Ansel disbarred provisionally on fabricated ethics charges and Elias suspended from the archive. Cut off from every official channel, they work from Elias's kitchen table. Beat: the law abandons them; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Letters
chapters.summary: Following a cipher reference to 'the light,' Ansel and Elias search the decommissioned lighthouse and find letters Coral wrote yearly to an unknown recipient, care of a post office box. Beat: hope — Coral lived, and wrote.

chapters.title: Delacroix Breaks
chapters.summary: Ansel corners elderly Marguerite Delacroix with the Renner evidence. Marguerite confesses the poisoning was done by Penn's father, that Coral ran rather than hang for it, and that the families have paid silence ever since. Beat: pity winning over loyalty.

chapters.title: The Post Office Box
chapters.summary: The box, still rented under a false name, yields a forwarding address up the coast. Ansel drives alone, aware she's likely followed. Beat: dread and determination in equal measure.

chapters.title: Coral
chapters.summary: In a seaside cottage, Ansel meets Coral Vane — old, sharp, unrepentant about fleeing, broken only about Tobias. She explains the will was her timed confession, triggered when her doctors gave her months. Beat: meeting the myth and finding a woman.

chapters.title: Penn's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Penn confronts Ansel with leverage: proof Elias altered archive records years ago to shield his grandmother. He offers Coral's quiet death in exchange for Elias's career. Beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Ansel tells Elias everything. He insists she publish, whatever it costs him. Together they decide truth isn't theirs to ration. Beat: sacrifice freely chosen, tenderness without guarantee.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Coral's full decoded confession, the pact, and the Renner evidence go to the state attorney general and every paper in the county. Penn is arrested; the founding families' names are read aloud in court. Beat: catharsis, and the cost arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: What the Law Couldn't Hold
chapters.summary: Coral dies peacefully days before her summons, having signed her true testimony. Ansel, reinstated after the charges collapse, declines to prosecute Elias's old alteration — some mercies fall outside the law. Beat: bittersweet peace.

chapters.title: The Reader of Her Will
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ansel's POV. She executes Coral's final bequest: restoring Tobias Renner's name to the town record and the lighthouse as a free reading room. Elias stands beside her as the plaque is unveiled. Beat: justice completed outside the courtroom, love chosen inside it.
